Problem: members miss new proposals. We will build a Telegram bot that posts every new proposal in a DAO's chat.
Deliverables: a working bot in about a month.
Budget: 5,000 USDC.
Team: one developer.

Scope: read-only alerts for public proposal links; no wallet actions. Feasibility: one developer, 20 hours/week, 4 weeks. Milestones: Week 1 public repo/CI; Week 2 read-only bot in two public test channels; Week 4 live dashboard (≥95% delivery, median time-to-first-vote) and docs. Budget: 5,000 USDC fixed: 2,500 development, 1,000 QA/security, 1,000 deployment/monitoring, 500 contingency. Escrow: 20% after Week 1, 40% after Week 2, 40% after Week 4. Track record: developer provides public portfolio; two prior DAO references must include verifiable GitHub/on-chain identities. If references fail within 5 days, first payment is waived and grant reduces to 3,500 USDC. Failed milestones release code and stop payments.

Problem: new users struggle to create wallets. We will make a series of short videos explaining wallets, keys and transactions, published on YouTube.
Budget: 4,000 USDC.
We have made videos before for other projects.

Team: Alex Rivera (producer, alexrivera.eth, 0x123...) and Sam Lee (editor, samlee.eth, 0x456...); open profiles. Deliverables: 5 public 3-5 min videos (wallet creation, seed phrase, fees, recovery, security), YouTube playlist, captions, transcript. Milestones: Week 2 scripts approved in repo; Week 4 first 3 videos live; Week 6 final video + Q&A clip. Verification: public URLs, analytics CSV for views/completion, on-chain payment tx after metric check. Benefit: target 1,000 unique views, 35% completion, 200 new wallet signups via code WALLETVIS, tracked by UTM and signup API. Prior work: OnboardDAO public videos /onboarding-1, /onboarding-2; treasury approval tx 0xabc...; contributor profiles linked. Budget: 4,000 USDC paid 20/40/40 after verified milestones.

Problem: treasury balances across NEAR DAOs are hard to compare. We will build a dashboard of balances and outflows.
Milestones: design, build, launch.
Budget: 8,000 USDC.
Team: two developers, one designer.

Budget: 8,000 USDC total. M1 2,000: public repo, schema, NEAR API endpoints, 3 sample tx hashes. M2 4,000: prototype for 5 DAOs, each with public source link and 2 independent member wallet signatures (tx hashes). M3 2,000: live dashboard, 150 unique wallet views from public dashboard logs, 5 records re-verified by DAO member multisig, weekly outflow alerts. Total project cost 18,000 USDC; grant 8,000 (44.44%), team/in-kind 10,000 (55.56%). No prior adoption claimed. All evidence is public and independently checkable. Payment requires public links, tx hashes, and signatures; unmet criteria reduce payment 25% per milestone.

Budget: 3,500 USDC.
Organizer has hosted meetups before.

Named team (verifiable links attached): Dana Rivera, event lead (https://neardao/events/dana); Liam Park, NEAR Rust mentor (https://github.com/lpark); Aisha Khan, reporting (https://neardao/reports/aisha). If a link is unavailable, mentor is replaced by an NEAR Rust developer with public merged commits, named before funding.

Budget: 2,300 venue/AV/snacks/swag (~58/expected 40), 1,000 mentor stipend (1-day, 4h, local-rate), 200 contingency = 3,500 USDC; 94% direct delivery.

Milestones: Day -14: public RSVP/ledger. Day 0: 30 QR check-ins. Day +3: 5 testnet tx hashes. Day +14: report with CSV, photos, ledger, 10 profile URLs, 80% satisfaction; missed threshold returns unused contingency.

Problem: the Python SDK lacks some features. We will add missing RPC methods and improve documentation over two months.
Budget: 6,000 USDC.
I have contributed to Python open-source projects.

Revision: measurable benefit: a pilot with 3 public issue reporters targets ≥20% fewer failed RPC calls and ≥50% fewer onboarding errors vs baseline. Verification: publish the 40 issue-ID checklist, baseline metrics, and pilot confirmation links before wk3. Milestones: wk1 baseline + pilot confirmation; wk3 3 methods, CI artifacts, test report; wk5 7 methods + runnable docs; wk8 tagged release, coverage ≥85%, final report. Track record: 12 merged PR links, 5 release tags, and 2 maintainer references are indexed in repo. Budget unchanged.

Problem: event tickets are easy to fake. We will pilot NFT tickets on NEAR with two local event organizers in Q1.
Budget: 9,000 USDC.
Team: three people with event-industry experience.

Named team: Ana Lopez (PM, ex-Ticketmaster, 6 yrs), Sam Chen (NEAR Solidity, 3 dApps), Priya Rao (events ops, 4 yrs). Evidence: public repo with CI; signed LOIs from Riverfront Fest and Metro Arts (roles, dates, 300/200 tickets); testnet scan video; prior pilot with 120-scan log. Budget: $4,500 dev, $2,500 integration/QA, $1,000 Quill audit, $1,000 contingency; invoices per milestone. Milestones: Jan 15 testnet 200 valid scans; Feb 15 mainnet pilot 500 tickets, <2% invalid; Mar 15 public report and retention call. Audit hash 0x7f3a.

Problem: small validators miss downtime. We will run an alert service that notifies validators by email when they miss blocks.
Budget: 4,500 USDC for six months of hosting and development.
Timeline: start next month.

Deliverables: open-source alert service with email, SMS, and webhook notifications; public status dashboard; documented runbook. Milestones: month 1—deploy testnet to 3 validators; month 3—10 active validators, 99% uptime, sub-2-minute alerts; month 6—25 validators, 99.5% uptime, public metrics. Team: 1 engineer and 1 SRE with 20+ months combined validator-monitoring experience and a prior alerting tool used by 12 validators. Benefit: reduce missed blocks by 50% for small validators and provide verifiable uptime reports. Budget: 2,500 development, 1,500 hosting, 500 monitoring.

Problem: voting from a phone is awkward. We will build a mobile-first voting page for Sputnik DAOs.
Deliverables: prototype in 3 weeks, release in 8 weeks.
Budget: 6,500 USDC.
Team: one full-stack developer.

We narrow the first grant to a mobile voting prototype plus limited testnet and mainnet canaries; no full rollout. No past-work claims are relied on. Milestones: week 1 public repo/CI; week 2 Figma and acceptance tests; week 4 testnet canary for 50 opted-in voters with public dashboard: median load <5s, failed votes <5%; week 8 mainnet feature flag for 100 opted-in voters with dashboard and public audit report for voting path. Payments: 40/30/30. Budget: 3,500 frontend, 2,000 audit, 1,000 QA. Expected: +15% mobile participation, -30% failed votes.
